Has anyone here been successful in growing a 3 sisters method crop? What advise do you have?

I have had fantastic luck with it. I tilled the edge of the gravel driveway where weeds were growing, mounded it, and it's doing far better than any of my neighbors corn.

Country gentleman sweet corn, purple pole beans, and acorn squash and loufa gourd. Mounded about three foot wide and a foot high, with corn planted at the corners of a 1 foot square with two bean seeds for each corn. Squash and gourd in the middle. Half a freezer burned redfish in each mound.

The beans have done a great job holding the corn stalks together, which is helpful against the wind. I lost half my corn to wind two years ago, none this year.

I'll post some pictures later.

Edit: https://imgtc.com/a/kM40XAn Corn is about 8 foot high, loaded with ears. I've sold several pounds of beans to the farmers market and am letting the rest go to seed for next year. I've got a couple of loufa gourds the size of watermelon and loads of acorn squash.

Wow what a treat! May I ask your zone and also when you planted your corn? Do they get full sun all day and how often do you water? I am starting a bit late, but in Zone 9 so hoping I have enough time to get this going, what are your thoughts about that?

Thank you so much for your time and knowledge...

I'm a zone 6b, and planted in early May. Part sun, with full sun from about 8am to 1pm, then dappled sun until about 3pm. Each mound has a .5gph dripper that I run for 20 minutes two or three times a week, but the mounds directly border a large pond and get some water from that.

I'm not sure about the time. I grew up in a zone 9,in south Texas, and corn was usually planted around April. Best bet is to look at the almanac and see your first frost date, and choose a variety of corn that will mature before then. Beans should be fine, I'm still planting beans and peas. Instead of squash, I would go with a variety of early maturing cucumber.
